ApiReference.title: convenr API
ApiReference.description: Everything a person can do on the convenr pages, as JSON over HTTP. Creating an event returns an admin secret, and joining one returns a participant token; each is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. A refused request gets an RFC 9457 problem with a stable `code`. Within version 1 a response may gain fields, problem codes and enum values, so a client ignores what it does not know. A request holds only the fields its schema names.

tags.events: Creating, reading, changing and deleting events, and their best windows.
tags.participants: Joining an event, answering it and leaving it.

security.adminSecret: The admin secret of an event, starting with `cva_`. It is returned once, when the event is created.
security.participantToken: The token of a participant, starting with `cvp_`. It is returned by each join.

createEvent.description: Creates an event and returns it with its admin secret, which cannot be recovered later.

getEvent.description: The event, its slots and every participant with their availability. The `ETag` changes with every change of the event; send it in `If-None-Match` to get `304` while nothing changed.

updateEvent.description: Changes the fields the request names and keeps the others. A schedule is replaced as a whole. When the change would remove slots that participants chose, it is refused with `confirmation_required`, which carries the number of participants in `losing` and the current `ETag`; repeat the same change with that `ETag` as `confirmedVersion` to accept the loss. The loss is accepted only while the event still has that version; after any other change the refusal comes again with the new count. `If-Match` is a separate guard: a change that sends it is refused with `event_changed` when the event has another version, so it never overwrites what the client has not seen, but it never accepts a loss.

deleteEvent.description: Deletes the event and every participant at once.

pickFinal.description: Picks a run of the event's slots in one day as the final time, or changes it. A weekday event also names the date of the one occurrence. Responses stay open. Picking the final time the event already has changes nothing.

getFinalCalendar.summary: Download the final time as a calendar file
getFinalCalendar.description: An iCalendar file with one event: the name, the description followed by the share link, and the final time in UTC. It never holds the admin link or a participant's name. Its `UID` comes from the event id and its `SEQUENCE` grows with every pick or change, so a calendar that imports a later file replaces the earlier entry. This is the only answer of the API that is not JSON.

clearFinal.description: Clears the final time. Responses stay as they are; a later pick counts on in `sequence`.

getWindows.description: Up to five runs of consecutive slots when the most people are available, as the event page lists them. A dated event's windows are taken per day in its reference zone. The `ETag` is the version of the event; send it in `If-None-Match` to get `304` while nothing changed.

join.description: Joins under a display name and returns a participant token. A name that is already used gives a token for that participant; when the name has a password, send it as `password`. To protect a new name, send `newPassword`.

removeParticipant.description: The organizer deletes a participant and their availability.

getMe.description: The participant the token belongs to.

leave.description: Deletes the participant the token belongs to, with their availability.

saveAvailability.description: Replaces the participant's availability as a whole with the slots in the request.

setPassword.description: Sets or changes the password that protects the participant's name. `currentPassword` is needed exactly when a password is already set.

removePassword.description: Removes the password after checking the current one.

getOpenApi.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the API.

schemas.Event: An event with its schedule and participants.
schemas.Participant: A participant. Nothing says whether they have a password.
schemas.Schedule: When the event can take place, tagged by `mode`.
schemas.RangeSchedule: An event on every day from one date to another.
schemas.WeekdaysSchedule: An event on days of the week, without dates.
schemas.PollSchedule: A poll of a few hand-picked times, each answered as a slot is.
schemas.Option: A time a poll offers: a start and an end on one date in the reference zone.
schemas.Slot: A slot of a dated or of a weekday event, or an option of a poll.
schemas.DatedSlot: A slot of a dated event.
schemas.WeekdaySlot: A slot of a weekday event: a wall-clock time in the reference zone.
schemas.OptionSlot: An option of a poll, answered as a slot is.
schemas.Retention: When the event will be deleted, tagged by `kind`.
schemas.RetentionUntil: The event will be deleted on a date.
schemas.RetentionKept: The event is kept until it is deleted.
schemas.FinalOpen: The organizer has not picked a final time.
schemas.FinalChosen: The final time the organizer picked, as one dated occurrence.
schemas.CreatedEvent: A new event and its admin secret.
schemas.Windows: The best windows and the filters applied.
schemas.Window: A run of consecutive slots when the same people are available.
schemas.Problem: An RFC 9457 problem: why a request was refused.
schemas.FieldError: A value at fault: in the body or in the query string.
schemas.PointerError: A value at fault in the request body.
schemas.UpdateEventRequest: The fields to change. A field left out keeps its value.
schemas.ScheduleInput: When the event can take place, tagged by `mode`. The server derives the slots.
schemas.RangeScheduleInput: An event on every day from one date to another.
schemas.WeekdaysScheduleInput: An event on days of the week, without dates.
schemas.OptionInput: An option the poll keeps, by id, or a new one, by its times.
schemas.NewOptionInput: A new option. An option cannot be changed; a new time is a new option.
schemas.JoinRequest: A join. At most one of `password` and `newPassword`.
schemas.SlotInput: A slot of a dated or of a weekday event, or an option of a poll.
schemas.DatedSlotInput: A slot of a dated event.
schemas.WeekdaySlotInput: A slot of a weekday event.

Participant.id: The public id of the participant.

Option.id: The id of the option, unique within the event.

KeptOptionInput.id: The id of an option the event has.

NewOptionInput.start: The start as an RFC 3339 instant at a whole minute, not before now.

FinalChosen.kind: Whether a final time is picked.

FinalChosen.slots: The event's slots inside the final time, in time order; for a poll, its one option.

FinalRequest.slots: The slots of the final time: a run of the event's slots in one day, in any order.
FinalRequest.date: Exactly for a weekday event: the date of the one occurrence, `YYYY-MM-DD`. It falls on the weekday of the slots and is not before today in the reference zone.

Window.slots: The slots of the window, in time order.

CreateEventRequest.description: A description of the event. Empty when left out.
CreateEventRequest.firstDayOfWeek: The first day of the week in the grid: 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. Monday when left out.

UpdateEventRequest.schedule: The whole new schedule, with every field of its mode.

JoinRequest.name: The display name to join under.
JoinRequest.password: The password of a name that already has one. A name nobody uses is refused with it.
JoinRequest.newPassword: A password for a name nobody uses yet. A name already used is refused with it.

AvailabilityRequest.availability: Every slot in which the participant is available, if need be included.
AvailabilityRequest.ifNeedBe: The slots of `availability` that are only if need be; a slot missing from `availability` is refused with `invalid_request` and the field code `if_need_be_not_available`. Left out, each slot keeps its stored level and a new slot is available. Empty, every slot is available.
